clue.text: Music to start the match

parts.note: the match is not a sporting fixture but a marriage, and this is the tune played as the bride enters the church

explanation.surface: A stadium plays a tune before kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport, but here it means a marriage: the piece played as the ceremony begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's or Wagner's processional tune traditionally opens or closes a wedding ceremony, which is a match in the sense of a union.

clue.text: One silly girl embraced by old politician becomes a plaything

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it, so the first pieces go within the politician

parts.note: a Whig was a member of the old British party that preceded the Liberals
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of girl are in a foolish disorder

explanation.surface: A daft young woman cuddled by a veteran MP turns into a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were a historical British party, later the Liberals, hence 'old politician'; 'silly' signals the jumble and 'embraced by' puts the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top or similar whirling toy is a classic children's toy.

clue.text: Distributed timber on time

parts.note: deal is sawn pine or fir wood

explanation.surface: Wood was handed out on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards or goods shared out among people have been handed round.

clue.text: At home, left with a wife and her mother?

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man at home with his wife and mother-in-law in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: a wife's mother is a relation by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's mother is a relative acquired through marriage rather than blood.

clue.text: Lady in the nursery rendering song verse badly?

indicators.note: something rendered badly is mangled, so the letters of song verse are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nanny murders a nursery rhyme as she sings it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SONG VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to teach and care for children in a private household worked in the nursery.

clue.text: A British tyrant lacking time — one to step down

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the tyrant word

parts.note: a dictator is an absolute ruler, a tyrant

explanation.surface: A British despot who somehow has no time left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes one T from DICTATOR, leaving DICATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who renounces the throne resigns, giving up the position.

clue.text: Study Georgia taking part in dance

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone examines Georgia's role in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American line dance in which people follow one another in a chain.

clue.text: Drugs that could make a star tubbier

indicators.note: could make suggests these letters can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Pills that might fatten up a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges A STAR TUBBIER.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sedative medicines, a class of pharmaceuticals once widely prescribed as sleeping pills.

clue.text: Girl in an organisation connected with TV

parts.note: the ITA was the Independent Television Authority, the old UK regulator of commercial TV

explanation.surface: A young woman working for a television company.
explanation.walkthrough: The ITA was the British body that regulated commercial television from 1954.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, standing for any young woman.

clue.text: Members of family could be old, even so

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become something else when reordered

explanation.surface: Relatives might well be elderly, all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges OLD EVEN SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Close relatives, those dear to us, are the people of one's family.

clue.text: Elite stream inappropriate — one is coming in barely able to read and write

definitions.text: barely able to read and write

indicators.note: coming in says the next piece enters the rearranged letters
inappropriate suggests the letters of elite stream are put in an unsuitable order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Putting someone in the top set would be wrong for a poor reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriate' rearranges ELITE STREAM, and 'coming in' puts I (one) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with only rudimentary literacy can just about manage words on paper.

clue.text: Shouter outside front of the building — where sound comes from!

indicators.note: outside says the shouter word goes around the next letter

parts.note: a bellower is someone who shouts loudly

indicators.note: front of picks just the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A loud man yelling outside a building where noise is coming from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes T from 'the', and 'outside' puts BELLOWER round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A church steeple or campanile houses the ringing chimes heard far around.

clue.text: Attractiveness of church member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: The appeal of a congregation's member.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma or appeal is the quality that delights and attracts others.

clue.text: Line up at the circus

parts.note: not a queue of people but a taut wire high above the ring that an acrobat walks along

explanation.surface: People queue at the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line up' looks like queueing; read it as a line that is up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A funambulist's high wire is a cord stretched aloft for balancing acts.

clue.text: Greek goddesses in a famous cricketing family?

definitions.meaning: the three Charites of Greek myth, deities of beauty and charm
W G Grace and his brothers were celebrated Victorian English cricketers

explanation.surface: Deities of Olympus turn out to be a dynasty of cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: W G Grace was the great English cricketer of the 1800s; his brothers E M and Fred also played for England.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglaia, Euphrosyne and Thalia were the mythological trio, and the Grace brothers shared a surname, so both are a plural of that name.

clue.text: Eccentric aunt Nora sheltering good little animal

indicators.note: sheltering says the jumbled letters surround and protect the next piece
eccentric suggests the letters of aunt Nora are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: little points to the short form: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A quirky aunt looks after a nice small creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' tells you to shorten good to its abbreviation; 'Eccentric' signals the jumble and 'sheltering' wraps it round the abbreviation. Orangutans are not small, so 'little' belongs with 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: A great red-haired ape of Borneo and Sumatra is a primate, a kind of beast.

clue.text: Mythological being to walk when head's been chopped off

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so the walking word loses its first letter

parts.note: to stroll is to walk in a leisurely way

explanation.surface: A creature of legend goes for a walk after being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's been chopped off' removes S from STROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian folklore creature, an ugly giant or dwarf living in caves or under bridges.

clue.text: Arrangement with bank on account of daughter needing means to keep afloat

parts.note: over can mean about or because of, as in a row over money
a raft is a flat structure that floats people on water

explanation.surface: A banking deal made for a daughter who needs money to stay solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep afloat' suggests staying solvent, but it is a literal floating craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowing beyond one's balance is a facility agreed with the lender.

clue.text: Scoundrel making European union go right back

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read in reverse order

explanation.surface: A villain makes the EU head back to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' applies to the whole string of three pieces, not just the last one, so the full run is read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest rascal or villain.

clue.text: Most foolish brutes, sad, torn apart

indicators.note: torn apart says the letters of brutes sad are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Sad thugs being ripped to pieces is the silliest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn apart' rearranges BRUTES SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of ridiculous: most ludicrous or nonsensical.

clue.text: Thin candle that a person carries

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to become gradually narrower towards one end
a slender wax light carried to light other candles or lamps

explanation.surface: A slender candle held in someone's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to narrow to a point, and the noun is a slim wick light used for lighting other wicks.

clue.text: Seeds showing sign of life

definitions.meaning: edible seeds of legumes such as lentils, peas and beans
the rhythmic beat of blood in the arteries shows someone is alive

explanation.surface: Seeds that show they are alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils and beans are edible legume seeds, and a heartbeat felt at the wrist shows life.

clue.text: European with one of his articles on a particular herb

parts.note: a German is a European
der is a German definite article, the masculine 'the'

explanation.surface: A German writes pieces about a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces; it means grammatical articles, and der is one of German's words for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall germander is a plant of the mint family used in medicine and gardens.

clue.text: "Wireless"? Not quite — I attached spokes

indicators.note: not quite says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: wireless is an old-fashioned word for a radio set

explanation.surface: A radio not entirely fixed: I attached some spokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of RADIO; 'wireless' is the old British word for a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokes run from the hub of a wheel to its rim, like lines from a circle's centre.

clue.text: How one may be taken by surprise!

definitions.text: How one may be taken by surprise!

parts.words: How one may be taken by surprise!
parts.note: completes the idiom for being startled: one is taken this way, as though pushed backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is caught off guard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'taken' plus this word means startled or disconcerted.

clue.text: Worked immorally and traded having collected one quote

indicators.note: having collected says the traded word gathers the next pieces inside it

parts.note: sold means traded away for money
one is the Roman numeral I
to cite is to quote a source

explanation.surface: A dodgy dealer sold goods after quoting a price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked immorally' means offered sex for money, the prostitute's sense; 'having collected' signals that the traded word holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Accosting people in the street to offer sex for payment is the prostitute's sense of the verb.

clue.text: A role that's isolated

parts.note: a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: A lonely acting job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set away from others is separate, standing alone.

clue.text: Stick with one seat possibly? Sure, if you have this!

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of stick one seat may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A fan wants to keep the same seat: guaranteed with this pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges STICK ONE SEAT; 'with' joins the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass bought for a whole year of fixtures guarantees a regular place at the ground.
